questions.question: How do you avoid div soup, and why does it matter?
questions.answer: Start with the semantic element that describes the content and use div only when nothing fits. Div soup strips landmarks and semantic roles, makes CSS brittle, and deepens the DOM.

questions.question: Which image-loading choices protect CLS and LCP?
questions.answer: Always set width/height to reserve space (CLS). Keep the hero/LCP image eager with fetchpriority=high, lazy-load only offscreen images, and use decoding=async. Use srcset for responsive sizes.

questions.question: What is the correct script and preload strategy for first paint?
questions.answer: Defer app scripts, async independent third-party widgets, and preload only critical fonts/CSS/LCP images. Avoid synchronous scripts in head and avoid preloading non-critical assets.

questions.question: Why does DOM depth matter and what does a good document outline look like?
questions.answer: Every wrapper costs parse, style, layout, and traversal time and complicates CSS specificity. A good outline is one h1, ordered h2 sections, and h3 subsections without skipping levels.

questions.question: What is progressive enhancement in HTML terms?
questions.answer: Build a working baseline in HTML — real links, form action/method, content — then add CSS/JS enhancements. The page remains usable if scripts fail or are blocked, with noscript for key fallbacks.

questions.question: Write a hero image and a below-the-fold image with correct performance attributes.
Why is preloading every script and image a performance regression?
questions.answer: Preload raises priority, so non-critical assets compete with the ones blocking first paint. Preload only the hero font/CSS/LCP image and let the rest load naturally.

questions.question: What breaks when navigation is built from divs with click handlers?
questions.answer: Crawlers get no href to follow, keyboard users cannot focus it, middle-click/new-tab is lost, and screen readers do not announce links. Use real anchors; enhance behavior on top.
